_comment: Per-category mode: enforce (refuse), warn (run, but tell the agent and log it) or off (no check). Every category is enforced: James wants it locked down. This file is the source; the installer copies it to ~/.local/share/agent-guard/policy.json, and `bazel run //tools/agent-guard:install -- --mode CATEGORY=MODE` changes the installed copy only.

git-history.covers: git rebase, merge, pull (except ff-only on the primary checkout), reset, cherry-pick, revert, am, bisect, tag

git-branch.covers: creating, switching, renaming or deleting branches

git-worktree.covers: git worktree add/remove/prune/lock/unlock/move, and rm -r of a worktree

git-other.covers: every other git verb that writes (config, remote, apply, clean, gc, clone, ...)

gh-pr.covers: gh pr create/edit/comment/merge/ready/close/review, and the auto-merge MCP tool

gh-run.covers: gh workflow run/enable/disable, gh run rerun/cancel/delete

gh-api.covers: gh api writes and GraphQL mutations

gh-other.covers: every other gh command that writes (release, secret, repo, label, ...)

lint.covers: linters and formatters run directly (gofmt, golangci-lint, ruff, eslint, prettier, ...)

kubectl.covers: kubectl writes (apply, delete, patch, edit, exec, rollout, scale, ...) and the kubernetes MCP write tools

bazel-cache.covers: deleting Bazel output bases (rm -r, bazel clean --expunge, --output_user_root/--output_base overrides)

guard-config.covers: agents changing agent-guard itself, or the files that drive session start

oversize.covers: a command too large to check in time (over 20,000 commands); split it up
